facts.text: Pacific Palisades was founded in 1921 by a Methodist organization, known for its seclusion, Mediterranean climate, hilly topography, and 3‑mile coastline.
The Kappe Residence, a Los Angeles Historic‑Cultural Monument since 1996, was named one of the city’s top ten houses in 2008 by the LA Times.
The Old Santa Monica Forestry Station, a California Historic Landmark (No.840), was designated on March 20, 1970, preserving early forest management history.
The Pacific Palisades Historical Society, founded in 1972, has archived over 3,000 photos housed at Santa Monica Public Library and transferred the Marquez Family Collection to Huntington Library.
Villa Aurora on Paseo Miramar, once home to writer Feuchtwanger and actress Marta, became the hub of the expatriate “Weimar by the Sea” community.
The Palisadian‑Post, launched in 1928, ran for nearly a century before closing in 2025, making it the longest‑running newspaper in Pacific Palisades.
